findings.checklist_item: Justify `remove_dependency` with a concrete caller and a rule-of-three argument, or drop it and implement relation-scoped removal purely by threading `relation=` through the existing `_get_link_info`/`_write_unlink`/`unlink_core`/`rebar.unlink` chain (reusing the one command-layer removal seam that doctor, the CLI, and the reconciler already share).
evidence: Plan: "`graph/_links.py` gains `remove_dependency(...)`, symmetric with `add_dependency`: validates the relation, finds the most recent net-active LINK ... writes the UNLINK event through the shared locked write seam, and removes the reciprocal link for `relates_to`."

Plan step 2 routes the reconciler through relation-scoped removal, but `_inbound_unlink_one` today calls `rebar.unlink` -> `unlink_core`; plan step 3 threads `relation=None` through `_get_link_info`/`unlink_core`/`rebar.unlink` — so relation-scoping is reachable without a new graph seam.

Today the removal path has NO graph-layer seam: `unlink_core`/`_write_unlink`/`_get_link_info` in `src/rebar/_commands/unlink.py` are the shared removal seam, used by the CLI (`unlink_cli`), the `rebar.unlink` facade (`_lib_writes.py:633`), and `doctor._unlink_edge` (`_commands/doctor.py:145-157`, docstring: "Calls `_write_unlink` ... the same event-writing path ... one level down").

`_write_unlink` already performs the UNLINK append (via `_seam.append_event`) + active-link validation; `unlink_core` (lines 136-145) already removes the relates_to reciprocal; `add_dependency` (lines 174-177) already owns `CANONICAL_RELATIONS` validation — the graph seam would duplicate all three.

Contrast (why add_dependency legitimately IS a graph seam): grep shows >=3 write call-sites — `link_core` (`link_revert.py:62-63`), `doctor.py:191`, plus tests; the removal side has no comparable consumer set.
findings.finding: The new graph-layer `remove_dependency` seam has no named caller and re-implements removal logic that already lives in the single command-layer removal seam (`_commands/unlink.py`): the net-active replay (`_get_link_info`), the UNLINK write + active-link validation (`_write_unlink`), relation validation (`CANONICAL_RELATIONS`), and the relates_to reciprocal removal (`unlink_core`). The plan's own steps 2-3 achieve relation-scoping by threading `relation=` through that existing chain, so the graph seam is not required by the done-definition.
findings.location: Approach step 1 ("Graph-layer relation-scoped removal seam") / Scope: `src/rebar/graph/_links.py`
scenarios: Implementer builds `remove_dependency` as a second removal code path that can drift from `unlink_core` (author/env sentinels, lock, reciprocal handling) — exactly the divergence `_write_link_event`'s docstring warns about for the write side.
A future removal-behavior fix must now be applied in two places (graph seam + command seam) to stay consistent.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer extending the existing seam: add the `relation=` filter to `_get_link_info` and an optional `relation` to `_write_unlink`/`unlink_core`/`rebar.unlink`, then have `_inbound_unlink_one` call `rebar.unlink(local_id, target_local_id, relation=relation, repo_root=repo_root)`. Only introduce `graph/_links.remove_dependency` if a graph-layer caller (parallel to `link_core`/`link_revert`/`doctor` for adds) actually needs it — and name that caller in Scope.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the blast-radius delta explicitly: relation-scoped removal removes a NAMED never-pushed managed link regardless of recency (today such a non-most-recent link survives via G5's permanent decline), and justify shipping this widening before ticket a4bd's discriminator lands (or bound it, e.g. gate on peer-confirmation for the double-related case).
evidence: Plan: 'This change only makes the outcome order-independent (the exactly-named relation is removed instead of "whichever is most recent, else decline forever")'
Code: `_inbound_unlink_one` today declines when `net_relation != relation` (apply_inbound_records.py:590), so a named-but-not-most-recent relation currently survives via permanent decline
2b16 ticket history: the analogous never-pushed-vs-peer-deleted inference is documented as state-indistinguishable and measured destroying 63 parent edges
Follow-up ticket a4bd (the discriminator) is filed but explicitly out of scope of this change
findings.finding: The plan frames the relation-scoped change as only making the pre-existing never-pushed-managed-link outcome 'order-independent', but it actually widens the set of never-pushed links that can be erroneously removed: today a never-pushed managed link that is NOT the pair's most-recent net-active link is protected by G5's permanent decline (it survives); after the fix a removal record naming that relation removes it regardless of recency.
findings.location: Plan section 'Relation to 2b16's fail-safe ruling' / Approach step 2
scenarios: A local dep whose vendor type collides with a remote link in the other direction (blocks vs inward Blocks) is never pushed AND not G4-protected; an inbound removal record naming that relation reaches G5. Before: removed only if it happens to be most-recent; after: removed whenever named — even when it is a second, never-pushed relation on the pair.

Neither appears in Scope nor Out-of-scope, indicating the inventory was not fully derived from the symbol-reference graph.
findings.location: ## Scope — `src/rebar/graph/_links.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/unlink.py` bullets; and 'Out of scope (owned elsewhere)' list
scenarios: doctor.py::_unlink_would_cancel — a consumer of the modified `_get_link_info`; if the signature/semantics shift beyond a pure `relation=None` default, this call site is unreviewed and could silently mispredict which relation an UNLINK cancels

findings.suggested_fix: Add doctor.py to the Scope/Out-of-scope inventory: state that `_get_link_info`/`_write_unlink` gain an optional `relation` with a `None` default so `doctor._unlink_would_cancel` and `doctor._unlink_edge` are unaffected, or explicitly plan to migrate doctor's pair-scoped-decline logic onto the new relation-scoped removal.

findings.finding: The fix converts the G5 permanent-decline (which fails SAFE: local-wins-and-restore, no local data destroyed) into an ACTUAL relation-scoped removal, without addressing that a removal record reaching this path for a MANAGED-but-never-pushed local link is state-indistinguishable from a genuine peer deletion — the exact data-loss class over which the parent ticket 2b16 deferred the whole removal-mirroring feature.

findings.suggested_fix: Include `src/rebar/_cli/help/unlink.txt` in the edit set alongside `unlink.py::_USAGE`, updating it to show `rebar unlink <id1> <id2> [relation]`.

findings.finding: The CLI's pinned help text for unlink lives in src/rebar/_cli/help/unlink.txt (a separate artifact from the _USAGE string the plan names in _commands/unlink.py), and docs/cli-reference.md is machine-generated from that help file under a CI drift gate; neither the help file nor the regenerated reference is in the edit set, so the documented unlink usage would stay stale and the drift gate would fail the build.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `src/rebar/_cli/help/unlink.txt` to Scope (update its usage line to note the optional relation) and note that `docs/cli-reference.md` must be regenerated via `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` so the CI drift gate passes.
